div.p: This value set includes codes based on the following rules:

ul.li:
Include these codes as defined in https://YasniiSS.github.io/fhir4eyes/CodeSystem/fhir4eyes-cs version 📦0.4.0
CodeDisplayDefinition
fusionFusionSensory fusion: the images of both eyes are combined into a single percept (e.g. a single pinkish light on the red filter plus light test, four lights on the Worth 4 dot test). SNOMED CT 78513008 Fusion binocular vision is an observable entity, not a finding, so it is not used as an answer.
corneal-reflex-centeredCorneal light reflex centeredOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex is centered on the pupil of the eye assessed, consistent with no manifest deviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-nasalCorneal light reflex displaced nasallyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced nasally from the pupil centre, indicating an exodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-temporalCorneal light reflex displaced temporallyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced temporally from the pupil centre, indicating an esodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-superiorCorneal light reflex displaced superiorlyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced superiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hypodeviation of that eye.
corneal-reflex-displaced-inferiorCorneal light reflex displaced inferiorlyOn corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) testing, the reflex in the eye assessed is displaced inferiorly from the pupil centre, indicating a hyperdeviation of that eye.

Include these codes as defined in http://snomed.info/sct version Not Stated (use latest from terminology server)

description.value: Qualitative findings recorded at a gaze position: sensory responses on the red filter plus light and Worth 4 dot tests (fusion, suppression of one eye, crossed or uncrossed diplopia) and the position of the corneal light reflex on the Hirschberg test (centered, or displaced nasally, temporally, superiorly or inferiorly in the eye assessed). The binding is extensible, so other findings (e.g. tropia vs phoria on a prism cover test) may be used when no concept here applies.
